title: Templo Mayor
visualBrief: Templo Mayor surviving main-pyramid excavation: nested low volcanic-stone construction-stage traces, interrupted terraces and west-facing stairs, the paired older Tláloc/Huitzilopochtli shrine bases under their modern protective canopy, two small mapped covers, pale plaster remnants, low walls and a supported visitor crossing. The main mapped below-grade footprint is an excavation, not a tall intact pyramid. Casa de las Águilas, the museum, cathedral and independent neighboring buildings remain separate. No hypothetical 1521 temple towers or copied narrative sculptures are reconstructed.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q774021/way1423783282 identifies the main-pyramid footprint. Four pinned standard PMTiles records control that below-street outline and three protective covers. Named map points fix the older Tláloc shrine to the north and Huitzilopochtli shrine to the south. The ordinary west-side picture establishes west-facing stair runs; the mapped outline/canopy edges give an approximately 5.85-degree east/south construction axis. Raw +X east,+Z south at heading 0; component positions beyond these controls are proportional visualization estimates.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: The photographs show surviving low terraces and damaged stairs, broad exposed floors and modern covers rather than an intact ancient pyramid. Construction traces rise 0.65–3.1m above the authored excavation floor; older shrine bases are 3.8m above it with short surviving walls. The main canopy eaves/ridge are 8.4/9.6m above that floor. Individual step counts, plaster patches, wall breaks, canopy joinery and artifact positions are estimates, not surveyed archaeological phases.
